question: In which of the following years was the SFURTI scheme launched by the Ministry of Micro Small and Medium Enterprises?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2005**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **SFURTI (Scheme of Fund for Regeneration of Traditional Industries)** was launched by the Ministry of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) in **2005**.
 
• The scheme aims to **organize traditional industries and artisans into clusters** to make them competitive and provide support for their development.
 
• SFURTI provides **financial assistance** for the development of clusters and **infrastructure support** to traditional industries.
 
• The scheme focuses on improving the **marketability of products** produced by artisans and traditional industries through product development and design intervention.
 
• It also aims to enhance the **skills of traditional artisans** through training and capacity-building programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME)**

 
 
• The Ministry of MSME is responsible for the formulation and administration of rules, regulations, and laws relating to micro, small, and medium enterprises in India.
 
• It aims to promote growth and development of the MSME sector, which is crucial for the economic development and employment generation in the country.
 
 
 
• **Cluster Development**
 
 
• Cluster development involves the creation of a network of businesses and organizations in a particular industry to improve competitiveness and productivity.
 
• It helps in creating economies of scale, shared resources, and increased innovation through collaboration.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Industries**
 
 
• Traditional industries refer to industries that are rooted in cultural heritage and rely on traditional skills and knowledge.
 
• Examples include handlooms, handicrafts, coir, and khadi industries.
 
 
 
• **Financial Assistance under SFURTI**
 
 
• Under SFURTI, financial assistance is provided for setting up Common Facility Centers (CFCs), procurement of new equipment, and training of artisans.
 
• The scheme also supports marketing initiatives, brand building, and participation in trade fairs.
